title: Clinic slot lookup behind a circuit breaker
name: Clinic slot lookup

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code uses the circuit breaker to protect calls to the EHR availability service? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
With the configuration in BreakerRegistryFactory, what happens when the EHR answers 404 for an unknown clinic id?
choices: It counts as a failure, because any exception thrown by the client is recorded
It is ignored by the breaker: it is neither a failure nor a success in the sliding window, and the exception propagates to the caller
It counts as a slow call and contributes to slowCallRateThreshold
It is recorded as a success because the HTTP exchange completed

questions.prompt: The breaker is OPEN and a request for openSlots arrives. What does the caller get?
choices: The CallNotPermittedException, which propagates to the controller
A fresh call to the EHR with the 3 second timeout, since the open state only logs
The most recent stored snapshot for that clinic and day, without any call to the EHR
An empty list, because the supplier is never invoked

questions.prompt: After the breaker has been open for 30 seconds, how does it recover under this configuration?
choices: It closes immediately on the next request that succeeds
It moves to half-open on its own timer and lets 3 trial calls through; the outcome of those calls decides whether it closes or reopens
It stays open until an operator calls transitionToClosedState
It moves to half-open only when the next request arrives, and then allows unlimited calls until one fails
